title: Ground-state phase diagram and route to supersolidity in a two-component extended Bose-Hubbard model
authors: Xuexin Qiu, Ning Bian, Yang Liu, Saisai He, Z. Y. Xie, Hong-Gang Luo, Jize Zhao
abstract: We investigate the ground-state phase diagram of a two-component extended Bose-Hubbard model recently realized with dipolar excitons, using the projected entangled-pair states. For the experimentally relevant parameter regime, checkerboard, Mott-insulating, superfluid, and vacuum phases are identified. These phases exhibit orbital-selective character, wherein the two components occupy different quantum states, but we find no evidence for a supersolid phase. The absence of supersolidity is attributed to the strongly interaction-dominated microscopic energy scales, which severely restrict the superfluid regime. Guided by the supersolid mechanism, we further explore a nearby parameter regime with enhanced hopping of one component and identify an orbital-selective supersolid phase. Further finite bond-dimension and unit-cell analyses establish the robustness of this phase. Our results clarify the zero-temperature phase structure of the dipolar-exciton platform and provide a possible route toward realizing supersolidity in this setting.
summary: The authors mapped the ground-state phase diagram for a two-component Bose-Hubbard model simulating dipolar excitons. They found that while the natural experimental regime suppresses supersolidity, by carefully enhancing the hopping of one component, they theoretically predicted and confirmed the emergence of a stable orbital-selective supersolid phase.
main_problem: The study investigates the ground-state phase diagram of a two-component extended Bose-Hubbard model to determine if a supersolid (SS) phase can be realized.
main_result: In the original experimental regime, no SS phase was found due to strong interactions suppressing superfluidity; however, tuning hopping in one component revealed a robust orbital-selective supersolid (CB-SS) phase.
method: The ground-state properties were calculated using the infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS) ansatz and analyzed with CTMRG methods.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by a two-component extended Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian, motivated by dipolar excitons confined in an artificial square lattice.
key_observables: Average density ($ho_\alpha$), density-modulation order parameter ($\Delta_\alpha$), and condensate order parameter ($\psi_\alpha$).
important_parameters: Hopping parameters ($t_1, t_2$) and on-site/interaction repulsion terms ($U, V$); the tuning of $t_2$ is crucial for observing SS.
main_assumptions: Components are treated as hard-core bosons due to large interaction strengths; calculations use iPEPS ansatz and finite unit-cell extrapolations.
figures_summary: Figures show the phase diagram in both the original (no SS) and tuned (SS present) regimes, illustrating the evolution of order parameters across different phases like CB-VM and CB-SS.
paper_structure: The paper first maps out the zero-temperature phase structure for the experimental parameters, establishing the absence of supersolidity. It then systematically tunes a hopping parameter to stabilize and confirm the existence of an orbital-selective supersolid phase using rigorous numerical checks.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the realization of exotic quantum phases like supersolidity in controllable platforms (dipolar excitons), providing concrete theoretical guidance on tuning parameters to achieve desired many-body states.
